newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Fresh food sales help Somerfield. [CORRECTED 14:27 GMT]
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Fresh food sales help Somerfield. [CORRECTED 14:27 GMT]

text.p: Increased sales of higher margin fresh foods helped supermarket firm Somerfield Plc boost gross margins in the first half of its current year.
Finance director Martin Gatto said on Tuesday dairy and delicatessen sales were up by eight percent, meat and fish by five percent, and bakery by 23 percent.
"Those are high margin departments...and the effect of that is to give you a better margin," he said told Reuters in a telephone interview.
He declined to comment on the outlook for the margins, but said the company had built up a momentum, which had helped margins rise over the past 18 months.
Improved buying terms as well as strong fresh food sales helped drive an increase of one percentage point in gross margin in the first half.
"We've improved our operating ratios in a very competitive market," he said, "And improved our gross margin when most others in the industry are seeing their margin decline."
Gatto said Somerfield had performed as predicted at the time of its August flotation, when its shares sold at 145 pence.
"We believe we've delivered the goods so far as the results for the half year are concerned...they're in line with most people's expectations."
The group held its position as the fifth biggest food British food retailer with a market share of about 5.3 percent, behind Tesco Plc, J. Sainsbury Plc, Safeway Plc and ASDA Group Plc.
Gatto said he expected the food retail market to remain highly competitive, but did not see a new price war looming.

The retailer has been converting old Gateway stores to new-style Somerfield and has converted 424 stores, leaving 150 Gateways. It plans to convert about 110 of these and sell or close 30 or 40 of them over the next three or four years.

Two new stores opened in the first half and another followed shortly after. Gatto said the group planned to open seven new stores in 1997/98 (corrects to delete reference to 100,000 square foot stores).
The firm is also experimenting with petrol station shops and has opened one already in association with Elf Aquitaine.

Capital expenditure in the half year rose to 66.2 million stg from 32.9 million in the comparable period last year. Gatto said investment had gone into systems, the Premier Points loyalty programme, supply chain infrastructure, training and advertising, and marketing.

The firm was created in a 2.1 billion stg buyout by Isosceles in 1989, but debts and trading difficulties forced three financial restructurings. The last in 1993 set up a holding company, which effectively shielded Somerfield from Isosceles' debt, leaving Somerfield with debts of 475 million.
Gatto said gearing had fallen to 50 percent down from 59 percent on a pro forma basis at the end of last year.
The shares stood 2 pence lower at 172 by 0949 GMT. -- Jane Merriman, London Newsroom + 44 171 542 7717
